title: The number of embryos a blastoderm forms is not fixed by genetics

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The number of embryos a blastoderm forms is not fixed by genetics

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The number of individuals formed by an embryonic blastoderm is not fixed at one by the genome: temporarily introducing breaks that informationally isolate islands of cells yields twins, triplets and so on, showing the blastoderm is an excitable medium in which several coherent embryos can self-organize.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Development: transition to multicellularity

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Indeed, the question of how many individuals are present in an embryonic blastoderm is not fixed at 1 by the genetics, because temporary introduction of breaks in the blastoderm (leading to informational isolation of islands of cell masses) results in twins, triplets, etc103.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: McMillen P, Levin M, “Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates”, Communications biology (2024), doi:10.1038/s42003-024-06037-4; section “Introduction › Development: transition to multicellularity”. Scope: Early vertebrate (e.g. avian) blastoderms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-collective-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Multiplicity after temporary barriers is an observable outcome that directly rejects a strict one-genome-one-embryo rule. Existing historical reports can test the phenomenon, but not fully resolve the dynamical interpretation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compile embryo counts and complete-body outcomes after temporary blastoderm barriers and compare them with sham manipulation and genetic identity controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The foundational experiment may lack open specimen-level data.

Physical separation demonstrates regulation but not uniquely an excitable-medium mechanism.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Embryo number after a defined separation is a direct count, and experimental twinning and triplet formation in the chick blastoderm is described with numbers in the developmental literature. Those counts are scattered in old papers rather than held as an open dataset. The contrast is informative for birds and incomplete for the full scope of embryonic blastoderms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In avian blastoderms of one genotype, introduce temporary physical or informational breaks and count coherent embryos versus intact controls. More than one embryo after isolation of cell islands, and one embryo without the breaks, would support a genome that does not fix the count at one; a hard stop at one embryo despite complete separation would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The published work is mostly chick, not blastoderms in general.

Cuts confound informational isolation with loss of cells and with mechanical damage.

Embryo counts after blastoderm cuts live in classic experimental papers, not a deposited table.

analysis feasibility: 0.32
